candidates.spoken: Two runes, merged into one symbol.
The Bluetooth logo is a Viking king's initials.
Bluetooth was intended only as a placeholder name.
RadioWire or PAN was meant to replace it.
The name honours King Harald Bluetooth, who united Denmark and Norway.
This radio link would unite PCs and phones.
Harald's nickname came from a dead tooth of a dark blue-grey colour.
PAN already had tens of thousands of hits on the internet.
So the logo merges Harald's initials in runes: H and B.
The planned replacement names were RadioWire or PAN (Personal Area Networking).
What is its angular rune for?

script.spoken: Two runes, merged into one symbol. Two runes, merged into one symbol. The name honours King Harald Bluetooth, who united Denmark and Norway. At an industry meeting, Intel's Jim Kardach suggested it as a temporary code name. Harald united Scandinavia. This radio link would unite PCs and phones. It was only a placeholder. RadioWire or PAN was meant to replace it. PAN was already everywhere online, and RadioWire's trademark check ran out of time. So the logo merges Harald's initials in runes: H and B.
